title: Patel v. Singh - Residential Deposit Withholding
factsSummary: A tenant sought refund of ₹50,000 security deposit after vacating a residential apartment. The landlord claimed deductions for painting and repairs but provided no receipts, inspection reports, or photographic evidence.
negativeFactors: minor wall scuffs visible in property

outcome.summary: Court ordered full deposit refund plus 8% interest. Landlord failed to substantiate claims and violated tenant protection guidelines.

title: Gupta v. Kumar - Legitimate Repair Deductions
factsSummary: A tenant disputed deposit deductions for structural damage to walls and floor tiles. The landlord submitted repair invoices, photographs before/after, and detailed inspection reports documenting damage beyond normal wear.
positiveFactors: clear lease provisions on damage liability
negativeFactors: no independent assessment by neutral party

outcome.summary: Court allowed 60% of claimed deductions for major damage, ordered refund of remainder plus 5% interest. Emphasized need for independent verification.

title: Sharma v. Desai - Written Loan Agreement
factsSummary: Lender issued ₹2,00,000 personal loan to borrower with written agreement specifying 12-month repayment term at 10% annual interest. Borrower defaulted after 6 months without communication.
evidenceSignals: formal demand notice sent via registered mail
negativeFactors: some delay in sending formal demand

outcome.summary: Court ordered full repayment with 12% interest per annum and ₹15,000 as litigation cost recovery. Lender's documentary evidence was conclusive.

title: Rao v. Nair - Informal Loan Dispute
factsSummary: Friend lent ₹80,000 without written agreement, only verbal promise and WhatsApp message saying 'will repay in 6 months'. Borrower stopped responding after loan date.

outcome.summary: Court dismissed claim due to insufficient documentary evidence. Judge noted absence of written agreement makes verbal loans difficult to enforce. Suggested arbitration or settlement.

title: Roy v. BSES - Meter Overcharging
factsSummary: Electricity consumer disputed unusually high bills. Independent meter inspection revealed faulty meter recording 40% excess consumption. Utility had not serviced meter in 7 years despite regulations requiring annual checkup.
positiveFactors: historical billing comparison showing sudden spike
negativeFactors: customer accepted bills for 7 years without complaint
no immediate action upon first unusual bill

outcome.summary: Utility ordered to refund 40% of disputed charges over 3 years plus 12% interest. Court emphasized utility responsibility for meter accuracy and maintenance.

title: Khan v. Water Board - Valid Billing
factsSummary: Consumer disputed high water charges. Board inspection found multiple leaks in customer's plumbing causing excess consumption, not meter error. Customer's recent renovation had introduced new fixtures.
positiveFactors: consumption proportional to identified water loss

outcome.summary: Court dismissed complaint. Billing was accurate. Customer responsible for property maintenance. Suggested customer fix plumbing to reduce future bills.

title: Verma v. Relocation Services - Failed Delivery
factsSummary: Relocation service agreed to move household goods on specific date with delivery within 5 days. Company failed to collect goods on promised date, delivered 14 days late, with damage to furniture.
negativeFactors: minor delay acceptable under industry norms
customer did not inspect on immediate delivery

outcome.summary: Court ordered 40% refund of service fee plus ₹35,000 compensation for damage. Unreasonable delay and property damage breach service standards.

title: Malhotra v. Construction Contractor - Partial Performance
factsSummary: Customer hired contractor for home renovation. Work completed but quality fell short of agreed specifications: paint quality poor, finishes mismatched, electrical work incomplete.

outcome.summary: Court ordered contractor to rectify major defects at own cost or refund 25% of contract value. Found material breach but acknowledged partial performance.

title: Singh v. Electronics Retailer - Counterfeit Product
factsSummary: Customer purchased smartphone for ₹40,000, advertised as latest model with authentic warranty. Product was counterfeit with non-functional features. Retailer provided no after-sales support.
evidenceSignals: customer complaint emails with no response
negativeFactors: customer could have verified before purchase

outcome.summary: Full refund granted. Retailer ordered to pay ₹40,000 + ₹20,000 penalty + ₹10,000 legal cost. Case registered against retailer with police for fraud.

title: Joshi v. Investment Consultant - Misleading Returns
factsSummary: Investment consultant promised 20% annual returns with 'no risk' on ₹10,00,000 investment in dubious schemes. Investor lost 60% of capital. Consultant's claims were not substantiated.
evidenceSignals: recorded phone conversation of false promises
negativeFactors: some risk disclosure buried in fine print
investor did not verify SEBI status

outcome.summary: Consultant ordered to refund 50% of losses (₹3,00,000) plus 10% interest. Court found partial misrepresentation but noted investor's due diligence responsibility.

title: Reddy v. Tech Company - Retaliation Firing
factsSummary: Employee filed sexual harassment complaint against senior manager. Two days later, was terminated for 'performance issues' without notice or severance. No performance issue documentation existed prior to firing.
positiveFactors: clear timing linking complaint to firing

outcome.summary: Reinstatement ordered with full back pay plus 6 months salary as compensation. Court found retaliation for harassment complaint. Company directed to investigate original harassment.

applicableLaws.lawName: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013
applicableLaws.label: Protection Against Sexual Harassment

title: Sharma v. Manufacturing Plant - Valid Redundancy
factsSummary: Manufacturing plant closed division due to automation. 50 employees laid off following legal procedure: notice period, consultation with union, severance payment, placement assistance provided.

outcome.summary: Dismissal upheld as valid redundancy. Company followed legal procedures. Court found no evidence of wrongful termination or discrimination.

title: Das v. Private Seller - Undisclosed Car Damage
factsSummary: Buyer purchased used car from private seller for ₹6,00,000. Vehicle had hidden frame damage and repainted chassis. Car failed structural safety test one month after purchase.
negativeFactors: buyer did not get independent inspection

outcome.summary: Buyer entitled to 70% refund (₹4,20,000). Court found fraudulent concealment overrides 'as-is' clause. Seller must disclose material defects.

title: Patel v. Contractor - Unsafe Site Injury
factsSummary: Construction site worker injured by falling scaffolding. Site had no safety barriers, inadequate signage, and untrained workers. Contractor provided no safety equipment.
negativeFactors: worker did not report earlier concerns

outcome.summary: Contractor ordered to pay ₹5,00,000 compensation for injury, medical expenses, and lost wages. Held liable for gross negligence in site safety.

title: Kumar v. Bank - Casteist Harassment
factsSummary: Bank employee faced repeated casteist slurs, exclusion from meetings, and unfair performance ratings by manager. HR responded minimally. Employee transferred after complaint.

outcome.summary: Employer ordered to pay ₹2,50,000 compensation, reinstate employee, and conduct mandatory harassment training. Manager directed to apologize.

title: Gupta v. Hacker - Identity Theft & Fraud
factsSummary: Victim's email hacked, used to create fake social media accounts and make unauthorized purchases. Attacker made ₹2,50,000 worth of fraudulent transactions.

outcome.summary: Criminal case filed. Victim received ₹2,25,000 refund from bank. Police case against identified hacker ongoing.

title: Rao v. Car Manufacturer - Engine Defect
factsSummary: Customer purchased new car, engine malfunctioned at 5,000 km. Manufacturer refused warranty claim citing 'misuse'. Third-party assessment showed manufacturing defect.
evidenceSignals: manufacturer's internal bulletins about same defect

outcome.summary: Manufacturer ordered to replace engine under warranty. Customer awarded ₹50,000 compensation for inconvenience. Manufacturer's refusal was unreasonable.

title: State v. Chatterjee - Defamation Case
factsSummary: Accused published false statements on social media accusing victim of embezzlement with no evidence. Statements went viral, damaging victim's professional reputation.

outcome.summary: Convicted of defamation. Ordered to pay ₹2,00,000 damages, 3 months imprisonment (suspended), and public apology. Social media content removed.
